# Learn Arduino — public website files

Source: https://learn-arduino-red.vercel.app/
Captured: 23 October 2026 (Australia/Perth)
Original author and on-page credit: Dilum Sanjaya

This archive contains 70 publicly served files (5,926,056 bytes before
compression). The downloaded files are preserved byte for byte.

Included:
- The English page and 11 translated pages: German, Spanish, French, Hindi,
  Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Turkish and Chinese.
- The deployed JavaScript modules for the 3D board, components, lesson
  thumbnails, 16 lessons, simulator and translations.
- The stylesheet, 20 font files, icons, social preview images, web app
  manifest, robots.txt and sitemap.xml.
- download-manifest.json: original URLs, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums,
  content types and the discovered file references.

## Open the copy on Windows

1. Extract the entire ZIP first.
2. With Python 3 installed, double-click START-WINDOWS.cmd.
3. Leave that window open, then visit http://127.0.0.1:8000/ in your browser.
4. Close the server with Ctrl+C when finished.

You can also open a terminal in the extracted folder and run:

    python -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory site

On macOS/Linux, use python3 in the same command.

Use a browser with JavaScript and WebGL enabled. Serve the site/ directory
as the web root. Opening index.html directly from disk does not support
the original site's root-relative paths and JavaScript modules.

The main application files and fonts are included locally. The original
credit links and canonical/social metadata still refer to their original
destinations. Lesson progress and preferences belong to each browser's
local storage; no visitor data was copied.

## Scope

This is the compiled public deployment, including files referenced by its
HTML, CSS, JavaScript and manifest, plus robots.txt and sitemap.xml.
It is not the original development repository. Unpublished source files,
build configuration, private server files and unlisted public files are
outside this snapshot. No source maps were advertised by the downloaded
application scripts. Original attribution and bundled license notices
are retained.

Verification: all 70 discovered public files downloaded successfully;
checksums verified and the saved application rendered its 3D board and
16 lesson buttons on a localhost server. ZIP checksums verified separately.
